phrases.text: Ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking.
Attention, passengers. A quick word before anyone changes their mind.
If I could have your attention, and whoever has the door handle.
Ladies and gentlemen, please put your conversations on safe.
This is your captain. The calm voice is included in the ticket price.
Attention in the cabin. Screaming will resume after the announcement.
Passengers, a quick briefing from the end with the controls.
Your captain speaking. Yes, that is what I'm calling myself.
If you can hear this, congratulations on the working headset.
Ladies and gentlemen, please remain seated and moderately optimistic.
Attention, squad. I have some reassuring things to say very carefully.
Your captain here. Please hold all questions until I've stopped talking myself into this.
Passengers, please listen closely. I don't have enough hands to do the gestures.
A quick announcement for everyone who mistook this for a good idea.
This is the cockpit. We'd like to thank the cabin for not touching anything yet.
Welcome aboard Cooper Air. We've never lost a passenger. We have misplaced several helicopters.
Thank you for choosing Cooper Air. We understand you had no other helicopters available.
Welcome to Cooper Air Combat Division. Every ticket includes complimentary small-arms fire.
Budget Air Assault welcomes you aboard. If you wanted armor, that was a different fare.
Welcome to Questionable Aviation Services. It's nice to finally have an honest company name.
Welcome aboard Definitely Licensed Helicopter Company. Please don't Google us.
Combat Zone Express welcomes you. Getting you there is our problem. Being there is yours.
Welcome to Rotor & Regret Airlines. The regret usually starts after boarding.
You're flying Cooper Air, now under new management following the disappearance of old management.
Welcome aboard Cooper Air. Our safety record is available on a need-to-know basis. You don't need to know.
Welcome to Budget Air Assault. We cut costs so the enemy doesn't have to.
Welcome aboard. The helicopter in the brochure was our helicopter's donor.
Cooper Air welcomes all returning passengers. Honestly, we weren't expecting this many.
Thank you for flying with us. Your fare has already been spent on a part we needed yesterday.
Welcome aboard Cooper Air. We're legally a shuttle service until someone finds the license.
Welcome to our luxury service. The pilot has wiped his hands on a nicer towel.
You're aboard Combat Zone Express. Our competitors take you away from gunfire. We found a gap in the market.
Welcome to Cooper Air. Our founder started with a dream and someone else's helicopter.
Welcome aboard Budget Air Assault. We've removed the hidden fees by making everything visibly terrible.
Thank you for choosing Rotor & Regret. Please remember that the second half of our name was disclosed.
Welcome aboard. We're the airline your insurance company warned you about without naming directly.
Cooper Air is proud to have served three generations of passengers in the same unserviced aircraft.
Welcome aboard Cooper Air. Our entire fleet is here, so please be nice to it.
Welcome to Definitely Licensed Helicopter Company. The certificate is drying as we speak.
Welcome aboard. The airline won an award for bravery. It was intended for the customers.
Thank you for flying Cooper Air. Your survival is excellent word-of-mouth advertising.
Budget Air Assault welcomes you to economy. First class is the same bench with fewer apologies.
Welcome aboard. This helicopter was purchased at an auction where nobody asked it to start.
You're flying Cooper Air. Our customer service motto is, well, you got in.
Welcome to Questionable Aviation Services. We were advised to put that warning on the ticket.
Welcome aboard Cooper Air. The company is in excellent health. The aircraft is a separate company.
Thank you for flying with us. We recently celebrated a whole week without changing our name.
Welcome to Combat Zone Express. We deliver straight to the part of the map other airlines avoid.
Welcome aboard. Our airline has a five-star rating from the five people who work here.
Cooper Air welcomes your squad. We bill by the passenger, so kindly stay the same number of people.
Welcome to Rotor & Regret. Please don't let the pilot's enthusiasm influence your legal decisions.
Welcome aboard Cooper Air. Our safety officer travels by truck.
You're flying Budget Air Assault. We offer competitive prices because nobody else bid for this route.
Welcome aboard. This aircraft was advertised as having one careful owner. It has had several others since.
Thank you for flying Cooper Air. Management would be here to greet you if this were safer.
Welcome aboard our family-owned airline. We don't speak to that side of the family anymore.
Cooper Air welcomes you. The paint is new, so please judge us quickly.
Welcome to Definitely Licensed Helicopter Company. The word definitely cost more than the inspection.
Welcome aboard. We're proud sponsors of the local helicopter recovery service.
Thank you for choosing Cooper Air, the airline with the most recognizable apology.
Welcome to Budget Air Assault. Your ticket is nonrefundable and surprisingly flammable.
Cooper Air is delighted to welcome you aboard an aircraft our accountant describes as still an asset.
Welcome aboard. Our grand reopening followed a fairly substantial emergency closing.
Welcome to Rotor & Regret. We put the adventure back into a trip that didn't need it.
Thank you for flying Cooper Air. The company photo has been updated to include the remaining staff.
Welcome aboard our premium service. The complimentary silence from management is especially reassuring.
Cooper Air welcomes you. We're the official airline of people saying it'll be fine.
Welcome to Combat Zone Express. Please don't confuse your destination with our recommendation.
Welcome aboard. We treat every passenger like family, including the ones we'd rather leave at home.
Thank you for flying Cooper Air. Every completed flight makes the bank a little less nervous.
I'll be your captain. Management has once again made the questionable decision to let me fly.
Your pilot speaking. I'm fully qualified under a licensing system I can't discuss in public.
I'm Captain Cooper. They gave me the rank because nobody wanted to be responsible for supervising me.
I'll be flying you today. My instructor said I needed more practice with passengers.
Your captain here. I was hired for my ability to say don't worry convincingly.
I'm your pilot. The person who was supposed to be here read the route.
Captain speaking. My experience is mostly in helicopters that aren't available anymore.
I'll be your pilot. I apologize if this is how you found that out.
Your captain here. I have several hours of flight time and a very forgiving definition of landing.
I'm your pilot and flight attendant. If you want a drink, consider what I'll have to let go of.
Captain Cooper speaking. Any resemblance to the pilot in that crash video is unfortunate lighting.
I'll be flying the helicopter. You're welcome to pray in whichever language works fastest.
Your captain here. My copilot is a sandbag wearing the spare headset.
I'm your pilot. My flight school has asked me to stop mentioning its name.
Captain speaking. I was the only applicant who didn't ask about benefits.
I'll be your captain. For legal purposes, captain is also my first name.
Your pilot here. Command said this would look good on my record, which is a low bar.
I'm your captain. The stripes on my shoulder are covering a tear.
Captain Cooper here. I also run the complaints desk, so think carefully about your tone.
I'll be flying you in. Nobody has agreed to let me fly them back yet.
Your pilot speaking. I was promoted for returning the keys. The helicopter was never specified.
I'm your captain. This isn't my usual aircraft. My usual aircraft is a landmark now.
Captain here. I got the job by saying I could drive anything with a joystick.
Your pilot speaking. References are available, but most would prefer not to get involved.
I'll be your captain. The company has described my learning curve as expensive.
This is your pilot. I get paid the same whether you scream or not.
Captain speaking. My medical certificate says I have a pulse, which put me ahead of two applicants.
I'm your pilot and the reason the safety briefing got longer.
Your captain here. I've been trusted with this aircraft until someone more qualified logs on.
I'll be your pilot. Please don't clap yet. It makes the achievement feel smaller later.
I've reviewed our flight plan, and I'm pleased to report that we have one.
This aircraft passed inspection after we lowered the passing score.
Maintenance has identified that noise as probably rotational.
I'm told we have enough fuel. The person who told me stayed at base.
I'll be cruising at an altitude selected to inconvenience both trees and anti-aircraft guns.
The warning light has been on so long I'm starting to miss it when it flickers.
I learned to fly from a video. The landing instructions were behind a subscription.
The mechanic said the engine has another hundred hours in it. He didn't say consecutive.
Don't worry about the vibration. If it stops, we're having a much bigger conversation.
My instructor told me to avoid unnecessary risks. He wouldn't define necessary, so here we are.
I keep the manual open to the emergency page. It's also the most coffee-resistant page now.
Maintenance found three bolts left over. They've promoted them to spares.
I passed my flight test on appeal.
The fuel gauge is stuck on full. Finance has never been happier.
The GPS keeps saying make a U-turn. It sounds increasingly personal.
My last helicopter is now used for training. Mostly the what-not-to-do section.
The duct tape isn't a repair. It's the original manufacturer.
I asked if the aircraft was airworthy. The mechanic said it was outdoors, wasn't it?
I've never hit a mountain. I've always stopped immediately upon contact.
That smell is either fresh paint or something we'd really hoped to paint over.
The engine was rebuilt by a man who kept saying probably while counting.
My copilot quit after discovering the dual controls were decorative.
I've disabled the warning buzzer. It was interfering with the warning light experience.
This helicopter comes with a full service history. Unfortunately, it's mostly complaints about service.
I know exactly where we are. We're at the little helicopter on the map.
The mechanic said to bring it back if the noise gets worse. Very encouraging use of if.
I've got hundreds of landings under my belt. Several were intentional.
Command says I fly too low. The trees have been even less polite.
Our backup navigation system is a passenger saying I think it's that way.
Don't let the calm voice fool you. That's flight school doing its one useful thing.
The engine has a lifetime warranty. Apparently this is how they decide its lifetime.
My flight instructor said I was fearless. I think he meant unteachable.
We've replaced the broken fuel gauge with a kitchen timer.
The maintenance manual has a thumbprint on every page except inspection complete.
I asked for a second opinion on the engine. The second mechanic stood further away.
The aircraft has been cleared for flight by someone who owes me money.
My license photo was taken before I learned what the pedals do.
We practice emergency procedures regularly. We don't always announce the practice in advance.
I thought the oil leak was bad until it stopped without anyone fixing it.
The compass points north when I hold it away from the very large gun.
I haven't forgotten the checklist. I've narrowed it down to the parts with immediate consequences.
Our mechanic used to build furniture. You can tell by the spare wooden peg.
I asked whether that crack was structural. He said everything's structural if you worry enough.
My flight test examiner wore a parachute. The test was supposed to be on the ground.
The helicopter starts more reliably when nobody mentions selling it.
Maintenance wrote monitor closely. They didn't volunteer to come and monitor it.
The cockpit has heated seats. We're still trying to locate the switch for that.
I always leave myself an escape route. The passengers keep sitting in it.
Command requested a smooth ride. I've filed it with the other ambitious requests.
I learned about lift in school. Nobody mentioned how much paperwork comes after losing it.
The tachometer has a red zone. I've been told that's where the warranty ends.
The spare rotor blade is a different color. Maintenance calls that easier to find.
I passed the vision test by reading the sign that said vision test.
This helicopter has excellent crash protection. The crash recorder is absolutely covered in padding.
I've asked maintenance to stop using the phrase good enough near the fuel tank.
The pilot's seat reclines. I discovered that during a maneuver I'd rather not repeat.
My emergency checklist starts with finding the checklist. We're improving it.
They gave me a map marked not to scale. That's an exciting thing to learn near a ridge.
I know the engine's limits. The mechanic told me while carrying the old one away.
The previous pilot left a note under the seat. It's just a phone number for a lawyer.
This aircraft was designed to survive enemy fire. Nobody tested it against our maintenance crew.
I'm trying a new navigation method called listening to the squad leader the first time.
I've never had a passenger complain twice. Interpret that however you like.
The flight controls are color-coded. I'm looking forward to learning the code.
Maintenance fixed the fuel leak by circling a smaller puddle on the inspection photo.
My instructor said good pilots are always learning. That's why I keep asking what things do.
Our anti-collision system is a windshield and my increasingly loud voice.
The rotor blades are balanced. One is expensive and the other was free.
I keep a fire extinguisher within reach. That's the closest thing we have to climate control.
My simulator score was excellent until it started counting property damage.
I requested a better aircraft. They washed this one where I could see them.
The mechanic described the transmission as brave. I'd have preferred serviced.
I know this route well. I've looked at it from several unusual angles.
The maintenance sticker says next inspection due. They've helpfully removed the date.
I asked for a crash course in flying. In hindsight, I should've been more specific.
The map has a coffee ring on it. Command has designated it a no-fly zone.
I can land this helicopter on a dime. Retrieving the dime is another matter.
The airspeed indicator is fine. It's the word maximum beside it that bothers me.
Our engine parts are locally sourced. Some from the field right next to the hangar.
My training included water landings. Mainly being told not to do them.
The helicopter's service manual has been translated from a language the mechanic doesn't recognize.
I asked how much weight we could carry. Supply said how much have you got?
The pedals squeak in different keys. That's how I know which foot I'm using.
I've installed a cup holder. Maintenance says it's our most successful modification.
My instructor used to close his eyes during landings. I thought that was the technique.
The emergency beacon works beautifully. We know because it keeps calling people here.
Our altitude warning is a branch tapping on the glass.
I passed the written exam. The helicopter seems more interested in the practical one.
The mechanic tested the engine by starting it and walking away at a normal speed.
I'm very good under pressure, provided nobody asks where that pressure is coming from.
The aircraft is missing a panel. We're calling it easy maintenance access until it turns up.
My flight-school diploma is real. The school was the questionable part.
The windshield wiper works. We consider everything behind it an optional upgrade.
I always trust my gut. It's currently recommending ground transport.
The mechanic has marked the loose switch don't. Concise, but incomplete.
I was told to follow the river. Nobody specified which bank I should avoid flying into.
The engine serial number matches the paperwork. The handwriting is remarkably similar too.
I don't make abrupt turns. I receive abrupt information.
We carry a spare radio so command can tell us the same bad idea twice.
This helicopter has state-of-the-art technology from a state that no longer exists.
The mechanic assured me the missing screws weren't load-bearing. He said it before I showed him which ones.
My last checkride ended with the examiner asking who trained me. He had trained me.
The cockpit door sticks. Maintenance says that's excellent security.
I called the manufacturer about that noise. They asked if we'd mind taking their name off the helicopter.
The aircraft's maximum speed was determined by the first thing that fell off.
I asked what happens if the hydraulics fail. The mechanic offered to demonstrate with my paycheck.
My landing gear is fixed. I mean it doesn't retract, not that anyone repaired it.
The mechanic said to listen to the engine. It's mainly saying we should've paid the mechanic.
I have complete faith in the aircraft. I've also memorized every field along the route.
The checklist ends with enjoy your flight. Nice to see somebody had time for a joke.
First class includes the same seat as economy, but you're allowed to complain about it.
Passengers on the left can enjoy the battlefield. Passengers on the right should probably return fire.
Today's in-flight entertainment is watching me discover what that warning light means.
For passengers making a connection, your connecting helicopter is currently on fire.
The flight attendant will be with you as soon as we hire one willing to board.
Our baggage policy is simple. If you can identify it afterward, you may take it home.
Repeat passengers get a free upgrade to people who should know better.
Cooper Air does not oversell flights. We do occasionally overestimate how many of you will fit.
The in-flight meal is a mint the previous pilot left in the cup holder.
Your seat cushion doubles as a flotation device if you have very modest expectations of floating.
Cooper Air offers complimentary earplugs. Ask loudly; we use them too.
The cabin is pressurized to exactly whatever pressure is outside.
All seats are window seats if maintenance has been busy enough.
Please stop asking for more legroom. There's a limit to how much helicopter we can remove.
Our frequent-flyer program rewards you for coming back. The first reward is genuine surprise.
If you ordered the vegetarian meal, the grass stuck to the skid is yours.
Passengers firing from the cabin are reminded that ammunition is not included in the fare.
The inflight movie is a war film. Unfortunately, we're in it.
Our complimentary drinks are whatever comes in through the door when it rains.
The safety card has been updated. The stick figure now looks a little more concerned.
If you feel sick, use the bag provided. If there's no bag, please aim toward economy.
Your seat reclines when the helicopter does. Please coordinate with the pilot.
Our Wi-Fi password is on the website. That should keep everyone occupied.
Cooper Air has never received a complaint from a missing passenger.
If you paid for priority boarding, thank you for testing the seat belts before everyone else.
The overhead storage is full of rotor. Please keep your bag on the floor.
Your first-class hot towel was used to check the engine oil. It's still warm.
The cabin lights are dimmed so you can't see what the mechanic wrote on the wall.
Our loyalty card requires ten landings. Bounces don't count separately.
The gentleman holding a rocket launcher has requested the window seat. I suggest we accommodate him.
For a small fee, the pilot will stop referring to you as cargo.
The cabin temperature is maintained by your proximity to the engine problem.
Our snack service has been suspended after a peanut reached the pedals.
The passenger survey has one question: would you describe the landing as over?
Anyone using the helicopter as cover should remember we're hoping to take it home.
The emergency bag contains a whistle. It's for attracting help after the loud part stops.
Our premium seats face forward. Economy discovers the direction gradually.
Passengers traveling with emotional support weapons must keep them pointed outside.
You may notice the lack of armrests. That was not an intentional design choice.
The reading light is the sun. Night passengers receive a discount on reading.
Your ticket includes a personal item. Fear does not count toward the allowance.
The cabin crew has asked me to remind you that I am the cabin crew and I'm busy.
We apologize for the smell. This helicopter has transported both soldiers and their ideas about laundry.
Anyone who packed a pillow has misunderstood the kind of extraction this is.
Our complimentary blanket is camouflage. We put it down somewhere and haven't seen it since.
The airline magazine has been replaced by the repair manual. Please pass it forward if you find anything useful.
Passengers with noise complaints may select a quieter battlefield next time.
Your life jacket is under the seat. The person who wrote that has never looked under these seats.
The cabin toilet is at the destination. This has done wonders for our punctuality.
Please stop waving at the enemy. They're already giving us plenty of attention.
Anyone wearing expensive night vision is encouraged to stay beside someone with cheap night vision.
The gift shop sells pieces of this aircraft. Availability is unpredictable.
You may upgrade to business class by declaring this someone else's fault.
The passenger manifest lists everyone as adult. Please try to support the paperwork.
Our seat selection system is based on who gets tired of arguing first.
The aircraft is fully accessible to enemy fire. Marketing shortened that to fully accessible.
Hot beverages are not served during maneuvers, which covers most of my flying.
Our return-customer discount was approved by someone who assumed nobody would claim it.
Your tray table is the person beside you. Please negotiate before serving soup.
Anyone filming should keep the horizon in frame. My instructor keeps asking for evidence.
The snack bag is inflated. That's more than we can say for the emergency raft.
If your bag falls out, please don't follow it. We already know roughly where it's going.
Our complimentary headphones let you hear the pilot in both ears, doubling your concern.
Passengers who enjoyed their last flight are invited to explain what I did differently.
For privacy, simply speak at a normal volume. Nobody will hear a thing.
The cabin has been deep-cleaned. We opened both doors and flew fast.
Our in-flight menu is printed on a single napkin. It says sorry.
If you're unhappy with your seat, remember that I have to look where we're going.
The first-class divider is imaginary, but please respect it. It's all they've got.
Our souvenir photo is available from whichever squad was watching us come in.
Children aren't allowed aboard. We already have someone asking are we there yet.
The passenger nearest the door has been appointed assistant gunner without a salary discussion.
Anyone requesting a refund should keep the receipt dry and themselves available.
Cooper Air no longer offers a money-back guarantee. Too many people survived out of spite.
Please keep voice chat clear. Your pilot can be confused perfectly well without assistance.
The premium meal comes with a fork. The standard meal assumes you've brought a knife for other reasons.
Passengers are responsible for their own valuables. The pilot is responsible for this very expensive argument.
The cabin music was canceled after everyone mistook the bass line for engine trouble.
If you recognize someone from a previous flight, please don't tell the new passengers how it ended.
Our beverage holder is a soldier who volunteered before hearing the whole request.
Anyone doing inventory should count the grenades quietly. I don't like surprises with numbers.
Our new loyalty tier is called Still Here. It's very exclusive.
The cabin has extra legroom today. A toolbox fell out.
If you brought a packed lunch, make sure the medic can tell which bag is which.
Passengers with a fear of flying may find the destination distracting.
The safety video features a much nicer helicopter. That's how we keep people watching.
Your upgrade includes a window that opens. The economy window hasn't closed since the incident.
Please don't feed the pilot during flight. He'll start expecting it on every trip.
Our baggage tracking system is the passenger who last said I've got it.
If you're traveling for business, please tell your employer we did our part.
Our estimated arrival is shortly before, during, or immediately after the firefight.
The flight should take three minutes. I've allowed four in case I find the destination twice.
We'll be there in a few minutes, assuming command means the marker currently on my map.
Travel time depends on whether the people below us paid for the express treatment.
Our estimated flight time is shorter than the safety briefing we decided not to give.
We'll arrive shortly. If you wanted a specific number, you wanted a different airline.
This is a short flight. Please distribute your panic accordingly.
The journey takes about two minutes by air and an entire bad evening on foot.
We expect to arrive on time. We haven't told anyone what time, which helps.
The schedule allows one minute for landing and none for complaints about landing.
We'll be there before your squad leader finishes explaining why it's safe.
Flight time is approximately three minutes, or one minute if the fuel gauge is right.
We're scheduled to arrive before reinforcements. Command hasn't clarified whose.
This trip is too short for a meal and just long enough to regret eating one.
The arrival estimate was calculated using a pilot who takes corners normally.
We'll reach the objective shortly after I stop asking which building.
Our on-time arrival rate improved dramatically when we stopped announcing departure times.
The flight will take a few minutes. Your squad's argument about the landing zone may take considerably longer.
Arrival is expected before the rescue helicopter would have got you here.
We should be there in the time it takes to remember which button gets you out.
The timetable assumes no detours around people specifically trying to kill us.
Flight duration may increase if someone spots a tank and everyone wants a look.
This is a nonstop service unless a very persuasive warning light comes on.
We aim to arrive early enough for you to blame command instead of transport.
The estimated flight time doesn't include the squad leader moving the marker at the last second.
We'll be there soon. I can already hear someone preparing to ask again.
Your scheduled arrival is an estimate. The ground tends to be more definite.
This route normally takes four minutes. I'm trying not to beat my personal worst.
We'll arrive before the fuel becomes a philosophical question.
Journey time is subject to weather, gunfire, and how much I trust the shortcut.
We're making excellent time for an aircraft that was supposed to be in the hangar.
The flight lasts long enough for a quick equipment check, not a complete change of career.
Command asked for delivery in ninety seconds. I asked whether they wanted us to land first.
We should arrive before the smoke clears. That's either useful or a problem.
The journey is almost certainly quicker than requesting a more qualified pilot.
Our destination is whichever landing zone currently has the least amount of gunfire.
The landing zone has four out of five stars. The fifth reviewer hasn't returned.
We're taking you to a lovely little firefight just outside town.
Your destination has been described as secure by someone asking for immediate reinforcements.
We're headed to the place with all the smoke. Apparently that's the invitation.
The landing zone offers beautiful views, excellent cover, and two blatant lies in this announcement.
Today's destination is close to local shops, public transport, and an enemy machine gun.
We're dropping you at the objective. The enemy has been kind enough to occupy it while we travel.
The destination brochure describes it as lively. Bring ammunition.
We're heading to a quiet patch of ground command has decided to ruin.
The landing zone is under new management. You're delivering the paperwork at gunpoint.
Your destination is the building with no roof. That should narrow it down eventually.
We're taking you to a field the map calls empty and the radio calls absolutely not empty.
The objective has excellent parking if you don't mind leaving permanently.
The drop zone is within walking distance of everything currently shooting at it.
We're headed to the side of town estate agents call affordable for a reason.
Our destination is marked with friendly smoke. Please remember smoke doesn't check uniforms.
The objective is lightly defended according to the heavily breathing man on the radio.
We're taking you to the place command zoomed in on and said surely.
The landing zone has been inspected from a safe distance. We're about to spoil that.
Your destination includes a complimentary walking tour of the nearest solid wall.
We're headed for the open field. By open, they mean everybody can see us.
The objective has changed hands so often the keys are on a lanyard.
We're dropping you near the enemy, as requested. The exact meaning of near is still being debated.
The landing area is suitable for one helicopter or several smaller pieces of one.
Your stop is a popular local meeting place for bullets traveling in opposite directions.
We're taking you somewhere with a much worse customer service department than ours.
The drop zone is conveniently located just beyond the point where I start questioning the route.
We're bound for the scenic ruins. Some of them are still being finished.
The objective was recommended by a squad that would very much like to leave it.
Your destination has a strict no-helicopters policy. We're delivering an appeal.
We're heading to the marker your squad leader placed before checking the height of the trees.
The drop zone has plenty of room on the map. We'll find out about real life shortly.
We're delivering you to a rooftop. The stairs were apparently too sensible.
The destination is a quiet village in the mission briefing and something else on the radio.
We're headed to an objective with excellent concealment. Nobody can find the entrance.
The landing zone offers a warm welcome, mostly from belt-fed weapons.
Your destination is in the middle of nowhere. The enemy has found it very successfully.
We're taking you to a position command calls essential and transport calls expensive.
The objective has received glowing reviews. That may be the burning fuel depot.
Our destination is suitable for outdoor activities, especially lying very flat.
We're headed to the empty courtyard. Please don't ask how recently that was checked.
The drop zone is right beside a road, so the recovery truck will have an easy time.
Your destination offers a choice of exits. They're all described as urgent.
We're taking you directly into the action. Please save your thanks until you've seen the action.
Please keep your arms and legs inside. We charge by the passenger, not by the piece.
Screaming is not considered navigational assistance.
Please familiarize yourself with the emergency exits. They're anywhere the helicopter stops being a helicopter.
Keep your weapons pointed outside. The enemy is providing enough holes for free.
Your seat belt should remain fastened until landing or until it becomes the main thing wrong with your situation.
In the event of an emergency, please let the pilot finish having it before offering advice.
Do not touch any red switches. I haven't tried those yet.
Remain seated. Standing makes you taller, not more bulletproof.
If you see a power line, say power line. Don't say oh, that's interesting.
Please don't shoot through the rotor. It's the one fan we all agree we need.
The emergency parachute is for the pilot. I apologize for the singular.
Secure all loose equipment. We don't offer air-to-ground delivery for individual magazines.
If the cabin fills with smoke, stop asking who brought a vape.
The tail rotor is not a handrail, regardless of how convenient it looks.
For your safety, please ignore the mechanic waving both arms until I work out what he means.
Do not remove your helmet for comfort. We're not that sort of comfortable airline.
If something falls off, tell me what it was before telling me how far it went.
Keep your feet clear of the pedals. I need both of those mistakes to be mine.
Passengers near the exit may be asked to assist with evacuations or become one.
Please don't throw empty magazines at the enemy. We may need something to throw at them later.
If you're going to lean out, make sure your belt has a better grip on you than your optimism does.
Do not unbuckle to look for your seat belt buckle.
The fire extinguisher is under the pilot's seat. I'm aware of what that says about our priorities.
If a warning alarm sounds, please don't add a second alarm with your mouth.
No smoking aboard. The aircraft has already claimed the allowance.
Your safety briefing is not optional. Only some of the safety equipment is.
Keep the door clear. It's our entrance, exit, and entire air-conditioning system.
Please check your grenade pins before making any sudden friendships with the floor.
Do not hang equipment from exposed wires. They're supporting enough decisions already.
The handles are for holding on. Anything that comes off in your hand was apparently not a handle.
If you notice fuel, describe where. On fire is also useful information.
Passengers are reminded that the helicopter is friendly even when the flying feels hostile.
Don't deploy smoke inside the cabin. I cannot land on a marker I am sitting in.
The brace position is demonstrated by anyone who has flown with me before.
Keep all fingers away from the door hinge. We count passengers by heads, but medics are more thorough.
The rotor wash will take your hat. Don't let pride take the rest of you after it.
If the engine stops, the quiet is not a luxury upgrade.
Do not use a flare to get the pilot's attention from inside the helicopter.
The glass is not bulletproof. Please stop explaining your aiming plan as if it is.
Please secure your backpack before it becomes someone else's helmet test.
If a door opens unexpectedly, don't try to catch the scenery.
In an emergency, follow the illuminated exit signs. Failing that, follow the man leaving very quickly.
Never approach the tail from behind. It has the reaction time and sympathy of a blender.
Please don't test your knife on the seat belt. We're currently relying on both sides of that experiment.
Keep your head below the blades. Your rank does not add clearance.
If you need to be sick, kindly avoid the controls. They're confusing enough in their original colors.
We recommend hearing protection. It also takes the edge off the pilot saying uh-oh.
Don't rest your rifle against the cockpit glass. It makes every head turn feel personal.
The safety card is waterproof. Try to remain close to it if we test that.
Please tell me about incoming missiles before telling the rest of your squad how cool they look.
Check your harness by pulling it, not by jumping out a little.
